text: The applicant complained of a violation of his right to freedom of expression on account of his conviction.
The applicant complained of a violation of his right to freedom of assembly on account of his conviction.
The applicant's conviction was based, inter alia, on his participation in several demonstrations.
The applicant's conviction was based, inter alia, on his participation in several press conferences.
The case concerns the alleged unfairness of the criminal proceedings against the applicant owing to his inability to question an anonymous witness at any stage of the proceedings.

The case concerns the alleged unfairness of the criminal proceedings against the applicant owing to the domestic courts' rejection of his request to have the contents of his confiscated computer examined.
On 29 December 2009 the Tunceli Security Directorate received an anonymous email.

The anonymous email received by the Tunceli Security Directorate on 29 December 2009 accused the applicant of being a member of the Patriotic Democratic Youth Assembly (Yurtsever Demokratik Gençlik Hareketi – the YDGM).

The Patriotic Democratic Youth Assembly (Yurtsever Demokratik Gençlik Hareketi – the YDGM) is considered by the Turkish national authorities to be the youth branch of the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan).
On 10 June 2010 the Malatya public prosecutor filed a bill of indictment against the applicant.

The bill of indictment filed by the Malatya public prosecutor on 10 June 2010 charged the applicant, along with eight others, with being a member of an armed terrorist organisation, namely the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan), under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237).
The bill of indictment filed by the Malatya public prosecutor on 10 June 2010 also charged the applicant under section 5 of the Law on the Prevention of Terrorism.
The Malatya public prosecutor noted that the applicant had participated in certain demonstrations in line with the PKK's instructions as published on certain websites and a TV channel.
The Malatya public prosecutor noted that the applicant had participated in certain press conferences in line with the PKK's instructions as published on certain websites and a TV channel.
The Malatya public prosecutor observed that the applicant had visited incarcerated members of the PKK to show moral support and undertake organisational activities.
The Malatya public prosecutor observed that the applicant had visited family members of incarcerated members of the PKK to show moral support and undertake organisational activities.
The Malatya public prosecutor observed that the applicant had been accused of being a member of the Patriotic Democratic Youth Assembly (YDGM) in an anonymous email.
The Malatya public prosecutor observed that the anthem of the PKK had been found in the applicant's computer.
The Malatya public prosecutor observed that symbols of the PKK had been found in the applicant's computer.
The Malatya public prosecutor observed that texts composed by members of the PKK had been found in the applicant's computer.
During the criminal proceedings the applicant denied the charges against him.
The applicant submitted that he had merely visited one of his friends in prison, who had not been convicted of any crime at the time of the visits.
The applicant submitted that his prison visits had not been related to any organisational activities.
The applicant stated that he had not received any instructions from any illegal organisation.
The applicant stated that there was no evidence to support the contention that he had received instructions from an illegal organisation.
The applicant did not deny that he had taken part in the demonstrations referred to by the Malatya public prosecutor.
The applicant did not deny that he had taken part in the press conferences referred to by the Malatya public prosecutor.
The applicant argued that the demonstrations and press conferences in which he had participated had been legal activities permitted by the relevant authorities.

On 23 June 2011 the Malatya Assize Court convicted the applicant under Article 314 § 2 of the Turkish Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) of being a member of an armed terrorist organisation, namely the PKK (the Workers' Party of Kurdistan).

The Malatya Assize Court's conviction of the applicant on 23 June 2011 was based, inter alia, on his participation in certain demonstrations on the calls published on websites and in media outlets controlled by or belonging to the PKK.

The Malatya Assize Court's conviction of the applicant on 23 June 2011 was based, inter alia, on his participation in certain press conferences on the calls published on websites and in media outlets controlled by or belonging to the PKK.
The Malatya Assize Court sentenced the applicant to nine years' imprisonment on 23 June 2011.
The Malatya Assize Court took the view that the applicant had been a member of the Patriotic Democratic Youth Assembly (YDGM).

The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had participated in various events such as press conferences, panels, meetings, and demonstrations with a view to actively maintaining the organisational activities of the Patriotic Democratic Youth Assembly (YDGM) in accordance with instructions given by the PKK.

The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in talks with other people concerning the arrests of other Patriotic Democratic Youth Assembly (YDGM) members which had taken place on 16 June 2009.
The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in a press conference held on 11 September 2009.

At the press conference held on 11 September 2009, the participants sent faxes containing opinions and recommendations of the PKK to the offices of the President and the Prime Minister from the Tunceli post office.
The document sent by fax at the press conference of 11 September 2009 had been known as 'the Roadmap' and had been drawn up by the PKK's leader.

The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in a press conference held on 12 October 2009 by a member of the Grand National Assembly of Türkiye from Tunceli in commemoration of the removal of the leader of the PKK from Syria in 1998.

The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in an illegal press conference held on 7 December 2009 in protest against the allegedly deteriorating conditions of detention of the leader of the PKK.

The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in a demonstration held on 7 December 2009 in protest against the allegedly deteriorating conditions of detention of the leader of the PKK.
During the demonstration held on 7 December 2009, the applicant had covered his face with a mask in such a way as to show that he had been a participant in the demonstration.
The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in a march held in Tunceli on 27 February 2010 in support of the workers of a State-run company (Tekel).
The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in a press conference held in Tunceli on 27 February 2010 in support of the workers of a State-run company (Tekel).
The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in a press conference held in Tunceli on 7 March 2010 in the context of the centenary of International Women's Day.
The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in the Nawruz celebrations held on 21 March 2010.
At the Nawruz celebrations on 21 March 2010, the applicant had been part of a group of Patriotic Democratic Youth Assembly (YDGM) members who had been committing crimes.
At the Nawruz celebrations on 21 March 2010, the applicant had – under the guidance of his co-defendant N.Y. – shouted at police officers for conducting a body search of a person named E.F.D.

The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in a panel entitled 'The 15th February Conspiracy' with a view to ensuring the continuity of campaigns organised under the legal appearance and in the form of rebellion.

The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in a press conference named 'We condemn the 15th February Conspiracy' with a view to ensuring the continuity of campaigns organised under the legal appearance and in the form of rebellion.
The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in a march held on 1 May 2010 to celebrate International Workers' Day.

The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in a press conference held in Samsun to protest against an attack perpetrated against A.T., who had been the then co-president of the Party for a Democratic Society (the DTP).

The Malatya Assize Court found that the applicant had taken part in talks with others about potential locations where Patriotic Democratic Youth Assembly (YDGM) members could meet and review its actions.

The Malatya Assize Court grounded its decision to convict the applicant on the visits he had paid together with other Patriotic Democratic Youth Assembly (YDGM) members to imprisoned members of the PKK to provide them with moral support.

The Malatya Assize Court grounded its decision to convict the applicant on the visits he had paid together with other Patriotic Democratic Youth Assembly (YDGM) members to the families and relatives of imprisoned members of the PKK to provide them with moral support.
The Malatya Assize Court grounded its decision to convict the applicant on materials found on his computer which had been seized by the police, namely the anthem of the PKK.

The Malatya Assize Court grounded its decision to convict the applicant on materials found on his computer which had been seized by the police, namely a symbol in the form of a star with the inscription 'Dersim'.
The Malatya Assize Court grounded its decision to convict the applicant on materials found on his computer which had been seized by the police, namely pictures of members of the PKK.
The Malatya Assize Court grounded its decision to convict the applicant on materials found on his computer which had been seized by the police, namely texts composed by members of the PKK.
Throughout the criminal proceedings the applicant maintained that the Patriotic Democratic Youth Assembly (YDGM) had been the legal youth wing of the Party for a Democratic Society (DTP).
Throughout the criminal proceedings the applicant maintained that all the acts imputed to him had been lawful.
The applicant appealed against his conviction by the Malatya Assize Court.
On 9 April 2012 the Court of Cassation upheld the Malatya Assize Court's first-instance judgment convicting the applicant.
